candidate: Argus continuous-handoff before_write split-brain boundary and boot-path fail-closed asymmetry

continuous_atomic_writer.observed_behavior: _atomic_write_bytes writes and fsyncs a temp file, snapshots the old destination bytes, invokes before_replace, and only then calls os.replace. If os.replace fails after the callback committed and the destination did not change, the code raises _AtomicWriteAfterCallbackError, which becomes ContinuousConfigCommitError.
continuous_atomic_writer.official_regression: tests/daemon/test_state_portable.py::test_replace_failure_after_callback_surfaces_instead_of_false explicitly makes the callback persist precommit.txt, forces continuous.json replace to fail, expects ContinuousConfigCommitError, then asserts the callback side effect remains while read_continuous_state equals the prior state. This mechanically establishes the generic partial-precommit state transition.

front_door_composition.observed_behavior: PreparedManagerHandoff.commit calls manager.commit_vertical_decision and records the goal contract. The continuous handoff supplies an internal _commit callback that calls prepared.commit, then passes that callback as before_write to the continuous-state CAS. The surrounding exception path marks the prepared handoff failed and rethrows as ManagerHandoffError; its finally block clears the pipeline-yield token.
durable_split_trace: Start from route/goal A plus continuous state A at generation g.
CAS holds the continuous lock and invokes before_write=_commit.
_commit durably publishes the Manager route/goal B.
continuous.json os.replace fails before changing the destination.
state.py raises ContinuousConfigCommitError; continuous remains A/g.
front_door reports failure and clears the pipeline-yield token; no compensating route rollback was located in this exact path.
Reachable durable tuple is therefore route/goal B with continuous A/g until later reconciliation.

boot_path_asymmetry.observed_behavior: Daemon boot also commits the Manager decision in before_write, but its broad exception handler immediately re-reads continuous state. If generation is still the expected generation, it forces init_continuous=False, clears init_objective and activates suppression for the old enabled generation before constructing the supervisor.
boot_path_asymmetry.scope_implication: The same durable route/continuous mismatch can remain on disk, but the just-starting boot process has an explicit runtime fail-closed backstop. This backstop must not be generalized to the live front-door path.

pipeline_yield_liveness.observed_behavior: The yield record is token/PID/timestamp bound. manager_pipeline_yield_requested clears invalid/dead-PID records and expires live-looking records after pipeline-lock timeout + 60 seconds. The live front-door finally block also clears its own token.
pipeline_yield_liveness.scope_implication: Requester crash does not imply an unbounded permanent yield wedge. This is a positive control and does not repair the post-callback replace-failure split.

reproducibility_assessment.judgment: The worker's refined diagnosis is strongly reproducible at source/test level. Argus itself contains a deterministic fault-injection regression proving that a before_write side effect can remain committed when continuous replacement fails, and the live front-door composes a durable Manager route/goal commit into exactly that callback position. The boot path materially narrows runtime risk with a generation-checked suppression backstop, while the live front-door clears its yield and exposes no equivalent compensation in the audited path. The audit does not establish real-world failure frequency or prove the worker's proposed handoff-fence/idempotent-persist fix.
